title: Native tensor comparison for the finite-free scalar model
statement: K-flatness implies invertibility of the native derived localization tensor comparison.

proof.text: Apply the K-flatness clause of internal_section_tensor_comparison to the pulled-back coefficient ring and the specified complex. Its right-to-left implication turns hK into the internal one-sided acyclic tensor test. The section equivalence here is definitionally ModuleRingedComparison.equivalence.

Use HomotopyCategory.kFlat_iff_preserves_acyclic. Represent an arbitrary homotopy-category acyclic object by a cochain complex and reflect acyclicity using quotient_obj_mem_subcategoryAcyclic_iff_acyclic. The preceding test gives acyclicity after right tensoring by the model; the braiding gives acyclicity in the other order. This proves native two-sided K-flatness of the model in the homotopy category.

Closedness gives sequential-colimit preservation by tensorLeft, and the braiding supplies the corresponding tensorRight preservation. Apply DerivedMonoidal.isIso_counit_app_app_of_kFlat_left to the native K-flat model and an arbitrary second complex. The lax tensorator of DerivedCategory.Q is the composite of the quotient comparison isomorphisms, this Qh tensorator, and the Qh-image of the homotopy quotient tensor isomorphism. Each factor is invertible, so their composite is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Finite free paragraph; F2 specializes the existing internal/sectionwise K-flat equivalence and the native derived-monoidal K-flat computation. The supplied hK makes a second finite-free resolution argument unnecessary.
